A man identifying himself as Alexander Smith claims to have taken part in covert CIA experiments in 1981 that allegedly transported him to the year 2118

07:00, 05 Nov 2026

A man wearing a mask and calling himself Alexander Smith claims he participated in secret Central Intelligence Agency experiments during the 1980s.

‌

‌

The self-proclaimed time traveller appeared on the hugely popular YouTube conspiracy theory channel ApexTV, where he "emerged with new details" about what the future allegedly has in store.

‌

Hidden behind a humanoid latex mask, Smith insisted the CIA sent him forward to the year 2118 back in 1981.

‌

"The world as we know it will change a lot and I feel it being beneficial to humanity to know not only about this change but also about the secret technologies being withheld from the public," he said.

"After my original video and after the second interview I did, in which I showed the photograph taken in the year 2118, I have decided it is time to share every detail of my experience."

According to the self-styled time traveller, Earth is destined to witness World War Three within the next hundred years.

Smith went on to claim that in the future, the vast majority of mankind will be packed into vast sprawling cities bursting with remarkable technology, artificial intelligence robots, extraterrestrial beings and flying vehicles. He claims this prediction stems from being told that a "conflict of interests" between the U.S. and North Korea would emerge in the not-too-distant future.

‌

"The conflict started off small; however, it soon spread, and Russia soon took the side of North Korea. Tensions began to escalate and eventually missiles were fired," he said. "I can't say where these missiles hit; however, I can say the effects were not what one may consider desirable."

He insisted the world began to come together as the confrontation intensified.

‌

"Borders began to become meaningless, and the people began to have a love and appreciation for life, one which would inspire them not to inflict any type of harm upon their neighbour," he said.

‌

"As a result of that, of the conflict, which some might describe as a Third World War, the world became a better place."

He further asserted that the U.S. government will supposedly disclose the existence of intelligent extraterrestrial life forms. Despite these remarkable claims, however, there is virtually no credible evidence to back them up.

Gary Horowitz, a physicist at the University of California, Santa Barbara, suggests that the concept of time travel isn't entirely implausible and doesn't violate established scientific principles.
